reasons: Relies on a matching alias table in the server that must be kept in step.

terms.meaning: The phase a project is in, such as planning, construction, or operation.
A named style group that decides a badge's colors.
A small colored label that shows a status.

sections.name: LifecycleTone
sections.title: Lifecycle tone names
sections.what: Defines the five style groups a stage can belong to: neutral, active, warn, dead, and retired.
sections.why: Keeps the set of styles small and consistent.
sections.watch_out: Adding a tone here requires adding a style for it below.

sections.name: LIFECYCLE_META
sections.title: Stage table
sections.what: Lists every project stage with its readable label and tone, and explains that operating and operational are the same idea and that retired is not the same as cancelled.
sections.why: The comments explain the reasons for these choices, which keep counts consistent across industries.
sections.watch_out: The stage list is also used for validation elsewhere, so removing a stage can reject valid data.

sections.name: formatLifecycleStage
sections.title: Readable stage label
sections.what: Returns the display name of a stage, or a placeholder when there is no stage. Unknown codes are turned into readable text.
sections.why: Users see plain words, not internal codes.
sections.watch_out: The placeholder text is shown to users when data is missing.

sections.name: lifecycleTone
sections.title: Stage tone lookup
sections.what: Returns the tone for a stage, with neutral as the fallback.
sections.why: Gives every stage a style even when it is unknown.
sections.watch_out: An unknown stage silently becomes neutral, so a typo will not show as an error.

sections.name: TONE_CLASSES
sections.title: Badge style table
sections.what: Maps each tone to the background, border, and text classes for a badge. Cancelled uses a red strike-through.
sections.watch_out: Uses theme class names, so changing the theme changes these badges.

sections.name: lifecycleBadgeClass
sections.title: Badge style for a stage
sections.what: Returns the badge style for one stage.
sections.why: Gives screens a single call to style a stage badge.

summary: Defines the project lifecycle stages, their display names, and their color styles.
purpose: Makes every project show its stage with the same name and color.
why: The comments say the list is the single source of truth, and that retired and cancelled projects are shown differently on purpose.
how: Holds a table of stages with a label and tone. Helpers turn a stage code into a readable label, find its tone, and return the matching badge style. Unknown codes are turned into readable text.
inputs: A stage code such as UNDER_CONSTRUCTION, or nothing.
outputs: A readable label, a tone name, the list of stage codes, or a style string for a badge.
risks: A new stage must be added to the table, or it appears as plain text. Operating and operational are treated as the same stage on purpose, so changes there affect both.
debug: If a badge shows a raw code, check whether the stage is in the table. If a badge has the wrong color, check the tone for that stage.
